action_text:
Matt Albert stated he is a resident of The Woods at Crooked Mile in Merritt Island; he is there to continue the discussion that was started by his neighbor Adrienne Vargas who spoke before this Board on May 5, 2026, regarding the growing Peafowl population affecting their neighborhood; Ms. Vargas is out of town today; at the May 5 meeting, Ms. Vargas provided a packet documenting the issues, including sounds, photographs, resident signatures, and information showing the impact of these birds are having on his neighborhood; since that meeting, they have made multiple attempts to follow up by both email and phone with Commissioner Goodson’s office, unfortunately, they have not received a response; they understand this is not a simple issue and they are not expecting an immediate solution; they do not know if anyone is looking into the issue or what the next steps should be; over the past several months his neighborhood has contacted Animal Services, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation (FWC), the Sheriff’s Office, their Homeowners Association (HOA), and so on; each agency has either said the issue falls outside its authority or referred them to someone else; meanwhile, the Peafowl population continues to grow and the impacts on the residents goes on; and today he is asking for communication about status and any next steps, specifically if this issue has been assigned to a County Department or staff member, if anyone is currently evaluating possible options, and if the County is unable to assist, could it please let the residents know so they can further focus their efforts. He went on to say their neighborhood has approached this through the proper channels; they have documented the issue, gathered community support, and followed every recommendation they have been given; at this point they are asking for a response and some guidance on what might come next; he expressed his appreciation to the Board for its time and consideration; and he would respectfully ask that a member of the County contact Ms. Vargas with an update on the status of the issue, even if there is not a solution yet, they would greatly appreciate knowing where things might stand.
Chair Altman stated he does not know if anyone has any comments; he knows he made an inquiry as a result of the meeting; he knows there is an issue with FWC and Animal Control; peacocks are sort of in the middle of no-man’s land legally; the Board probably needs to provide the residents with more information; he is glad Mr. Albert is here; and staff will get on it. He definitely thinks this is an action item the Board needs to act on.
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, stated there is a bunch of discussion; the minutes happened to be there but he has not gotten to the end, but it kind of looked like it just went there, but staff will come up with some kind of follow up.
Chair Altman stated that there needs to be some kind of response and he appreciated that being brought up; his aide is back there; he knows staff is here; and someone will get them an answer on that. He noted he hit one with his car one afternoon, it walked right in front of him; he could not sleep that night, he felt bad; he thinks it survived, those are tough animals; it dented his car; he got out to find it, but it had run away; but he will have someone follow up.
Sandra Sullivan stated happy 250th anniversary to this great nation; as Benjamin Franklin said, “A republic, if you can keep it.” She stated there are a lot of people who share her concerns about data centers and the mass surveillance, and the digital currency risks that that would bring to this society; now there are 20 counties and municipalities that have done moratoriums on hyperscale data centers; she is requesting Brevard County to consider a moratorium on these data centers; Economic Development Council (EDC) is in emails for data centers in Brevard; she is hearing potential plans at Titusville-Cocoa Airport (TICO) and perhaps Palm Bay compound; EDC gets 12 months of records request exemptions; and she is hearing about Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) in Titusville. She went on to say Brevard County officially voted to approve legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance excluding data centers from receiving economic development property tax abatements on April 7, 2026, but the Board has not advertised legislative intent, so she would like an update on that; she asked if Brevard County violated the law when it did not go to legislative intent before the vote on December 17, 2024, which gave data centers 20 years tax exemptions; under Florida Statutes 196.1995, when Brevard County voters passed a referendum on November 5, 2024, they voted for very specific strictly bound constitutional authority; the Statute says any ad valorem tax exemption granted by a county board under this program cannot exceed 10 years, but this Board did 20 years; and on November 5, 2024, the voters approved the tax exemption abatement for the EDC, would voters have voted for the EDC tax abatement if it included 20 years tax exemption for data centers, she thinks not. She commented it looks like a bait and switch; right after that referendum, on December 17, right before Christmas when everybody is busy with their holidays, with Commissioner Feltner then on the EDC Board and was Chair of the Board of County Commissioners (BoCC), they changed the ordinance for a 20-year tax exempt for data centers; as established by Florida Statute 125.66 which says one cannot change an ordinance without first going out to legislative intent for a voter referendum, the BoCC quietly granted data centers an unprecedented 20-year timeline without a formal advertised public hearing cycle, alleged, in violation of Florida law; and she would like the Board consideration to correct these things and get a moratorium on data centers, hyperscale.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing for an ordinance amending the Brevard County local provider participation fund no-ad valorem assessment to address waiver exemptions and allow for the opportunity for local hospitals to participate in managed care quality incentive program.
Morris Richardson, County attorney, stated Brevard County levies a local provider participation fund non-ad valorem assessment on hospitals to fund Medicaid payments for those hospitals who provide services to low-income and Medicaid eligible citizens; hospitals pay the assessment to the County and we transfer the funds to the State where they qualify for federal match; this assessment cost local taxpayers nothing and the hospitals actually requested that the County implement it because the benefits flow to those hospitals increasing reimbursement for Medicaid services and eligible care; and this ordinance updates the assessment structure in order to address the One Big Beautiful Bill Act which affected how states can finance Medicaid programs. He continued by saying it incorporates certain waiver provisions that exempt some facilities from provide taxes; it also allows for the opportunity to participate in a new managed care quality incentive program in addition to the existing Medicaid payment programs already funded by the assessment; it does not affect the assessment rate which is set by resolution after public notice and a public hearing; and the same hospitals that requested the County’s enactment of the assessment in the first instance, have requested this ordinance and the updates it would make to the program. He noted he believes someone representing those hospital interests is here and has submitted a speaker card if the Board has any questions.
Chair Altman advised he has that card for questions only and he has another card for Stephen Lord; and he asked if he would like to speak.
Stephen Lord stated he will wave in support.
Colleen Ernst stated she is the technical expert on the Item so if there are any questions from the Board she would be happy to answer those, otherwise, she is happy to be there in support.
Chair Altman stated that is a fantastic program.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she would make a motion to approve as written.
Sandra Sullivan stated she wanted to remind the Board when this was initially voted on as a formal hearing, the proper notice was not given and the date that it was advertised on was a later date than what the hearing was; and there does appear to be some impropriety there.
Chair Altman stated there is an allegation of impropriety, and asked if there is any substance to that.
Morris Richardson, County Attorney, responded by saying no.
Commissioner Feltner stated he will second.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board conducted the public hearing and adopted Ordinance No. 26-07, amending the Brevard County Local Provider Participation Fund Non-Ad Valorem Assessment to address waiver exemptions and allow for the opportunity for local hospitals to participate in managed care quality incentive program.

action_text:
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, stated he will handle the first part; this is being brought back as the Board voted back in February to remove the design credit off of folks stormwater fees if they were eligible for it and begin the process of that; that would generate about $850,000 per year; they are in the process of starting to notify homeowners; in between the February vote and what happened on June 1, 2, and 3, the Legislature put the amendment number 3 on the ballot; the stormwater assessment helps build projects, but a good majority of the funding for maintenance and drainage comes from the Road and Bridge Municipal Service Taxing Units (MSTUs); and based on some of the numbers they are seeing from the Property Appraiser’s, if the voters voted for amendment 3, the County would lose about $2 million in revenue from the MSTUs; that is how the County maintains a lot of the stormwater and drainage; and staff wanted to bring this back for discussion to see if the Board is willing to talk about putting off the design credit notification in the process until they see what the November vote will bring. He went on to say, if the November vote happens, there will be a lot of changes, structural changes, to the budget and the County on how to provide services; luckily this is core service, but there may not be enough funding to go around; and there are a number of options, but staff is looking at Option 1, asking if the Board could direct staff to schedule an Item during the Fiscal Year 2026/2027 to consider adoption of stormwater assessment rate amendments following the referendum.
Sandra Sullivan stated what she just heard Mr. Liesenfelt say is that the Board will wait until after the referendum to decide about the rate increases; there have been a couple conversations here on the dais about increasing stormwater fees to address flooding; a lot of flooding was identified in District 1; there was flooding up there just yesterday; also in District 2; she thinks there also needs to be some real conversations about cause and effect and looking at not just putting the burden of rate increases on the people; Commissioner Feltner had mentioned, when it was brought up by Commissioner Delaney, about addressing putting some funds from the budget to addressing that; there was a commitment made to allocate some funds from the Lagoon tax, reprioritize some of that to address that need, and that conversation did not ensue, so that is certainly one avenue; and she would like to note that there is $9 million plus in appropriations for some stormwater projects up in District 1 which is great to see. She mentioned it is very important to address stormwater especially if it affects the Lagoon because it lowers the salinity and the seagrass does not grow, where the Lagoon tax can be adjusted; she thinks the scientists agree that the freshwater impacts the Lagoon and that funding could be utilized; another thing is space; she has been at meetings with Commissioner Goodson, plus there is a one-half million hydrology study showing tremendous impact, millions of dollars of impact of flooding coming as Space Florida brings in fill and how that is affecting the flow to District 2 and North Merritt Island; and she thinks it is time to have a real conversation about space paying stormwater fees, and for the impact that they have on their neighbors. She commented it is not fair for people who are saying that their property is becoming worthless; there are some conversations that need to be had on this and then it goes back to impact fees; and her last point is that the Board had an opportunity prior to July 1 to increase impact fees with the feasibility study and by delaying it until after July 1, the Board has taken away an opportunity and limiting how much the Board can increase that, which has not been increased in over 25 years.
Rick Heffelfinger stated this one is really complicated and confusing because it stemmed from a discussion that the Board had back on February 24, Item I.2.; the Board put forward this idea that it was going to do possibly six things; the result of that vote, if he is correct, is decided not to do anything with one, three, four, and six, but did decide to eliminate the design credit only; the Board did not raise the fee on everybody that was going to create $2.4 million; everyone was happy for not getting more fees and having to pay for this stuff; and the design credit is a weird thing because it seems that the design credit impacts District 4 by $593,000 and only impacts District 1 by $37,331. He commented he would guess a bunch of people in District 4 are getting those credits somehow; do they have ponds on their property, he does not know; he does not think Commissioner Feltner was in favor of that when it voted for number two; the Board waved off three which was $2.4 million; the Board also had the conversation about the revenue split, so when those MSTU values come in, and he thinks Commissioner Adkinson brought it up and Commissioner Delaney was interested in that, but then it was said that the Board could not really decide that now, it needs to have more conversations because it may be legally, the Board changing how that money is spent, maybe it needs to notify or something, and he thinks the County Attorney had some input on that; and he asked if the Board votes on this now, is it ever going to talk about the split issue again, or should it wait, his recommendation would be to wait and pick option 1 to put this off and when it is brought back up, to have already have that split conversation decided; why spend $120,000 on mailings when it is not addressing the split; he mentioned he does not think they should waste that money; the County is only receiving $857,000 and that does not even buy a nice house any longer, so the return on investment is not very good; and he thinks the Board needs to discuss the split. He reiterated that is his recommendation chose option 1 and do not do anything.
Chair Altman stated that is kind of what the recommendation is.
Commissioner Adkinson advised she has some discussion; she stands by her vote last time which was to remove the design credits and increase the minimum collection; a lot of what people have said in the conversations that she has had, she is wondering if the Board should not do a little bit more right now because justifying the increase, talking about the split, maybe the Board should find out more facts before deciding what it is actually going to do here; she asked what is the sense of increasing it now and then later having to do it again if it is not enough; does the Board have a study done to get some of the facts before doing this; and she mentioned she does not know, she is just having a conversation right now. She continued by saying she does not know if there is anybody on staff who wants to comment or what her fellow Commissioners think.
Chair Altman stated maybe have staff provide a little information or background.
Virginia Barker, Natural Resources Management Director, stated there was a rate study last time the Board changed the stormwater fee; that could be done again; it could include in the scope to look at the maintenance needs that the County Manager described with MSTU; all of that could be taken into account; it would probably take about six months, cost on the order of about $150,000; and staff could bring it back to the Board in early 2027, in time to send notices out by next summer.
Commissioner Feltner asked if he could clarify that that is just a rate study.
Ms. Barker replied affirmatively.
Commissioner Feltner stated it is largely a survey of other municipal governments, surrounding counties, all of that to figure out that Brevard County is somewhere in the middle, or low, or high; how the assesses it; and he asked if that is what the rate study does.
Morris Richardson, County Attorney, explained an assessment rate study looks at the benefit that is conferred by the program, the cost of providing the program, and how it is apportioned among those that pay in the program; what slice of that benefit each is receiving; it decides how it is apportioned, it could be based on things like pervious square footage on a property, or the drainage improvements existing on the property, like the current design credit; and all those factors are taken into effect and they try to do rough justice to apportioning the cost of that program to the rate payers who pay into it.
Ms. Barker noted they can do forecasting, looking at more of the long-term needs and how to apportion that and provide alternatives; they can also assist with public information, workshops if the Board wants that; and those rate study scopes vary from community to community depending on what all the Board wants included.
Commissioner Feltner inquired if there are any of those that are done by another County, municipal government, Department of Environmental Protect (DEP), or St. Johns River Water Management District (SJRWMD), that this Board could adopt and not have to spend over $100,000 for a separate study. He noted he understands it is Brevard County…
Ms. Barker responded they are very area specific; she stated the most recent similar one was Clay County last year and that cost $148,000; that is a County and an existing stormwater utility, not looking at establishing a new one; and they did rate modeling and public outreach.
Commissioner Adkinson asked when the last rate study was done.
Ms. Barker replied 2013, before the Board adopted changes in 2014.
Attorney Richardson stated it is possible that rather than a study, staff needs to look at the overall cost of the program, and Board can keep the methodology of the existing study and assessment, and just look at what rates should be in order to fund the cost of the program today.
Ms. Barker agreed; she stated the County has the roles and the impervious area so staff may be able to pare down the scope considerably; and she is not sure what all Clay County had to work with.
Commissioner Adkinson commented she is not crazy about spending money on studies at all, but she is also not comfortable just saying to do this without having it specific to Brevard; and if the last one was done in 2013, that is a while ago.
Commissioner Feltner stated if the Board is done with questions, his comment is tonight he would go with option 1, then the Board could consider some study in the future as staff mentioned it is not just the referendum, but all of the implementing language that will come in December, when the Board can better consider things; of course, he was on the other side of this vote, as the Board knows; it was not something he wanted to do at that time; and if the Board does not do this and agreed on that tonight, that is where he would be. He stated he will make a motion for option 1.
Commissioner Goodson stated he will second the motion.
Chair Altman inquired if the Board needs a motion for reconsideration, the parliamentary procedure, it has to be from a prevailing party.
Attorney Richardson responded that technically under Robert’s Rules, that applies at the same meeting, a motion for reconsideration; what has been done in the past to prevent Items from coming up ad nauseam; he thinks this one the posture is a little bit different because there are intermediary steps; he thinks staff is looking for direction now on whether to do the mailer, therefore, he was not inclined to say that is required; however, if the Board wanted to, just as a formality, it could say for purposes of entertaining this, it is going to waive Robert’s Rules of Parliamentary Procedure for this Item and entertain a motion to reconsider. He noted he will leave that to the discretion of the Chair.
Chair Altman stated he is fine, there is an intermediary, time has passed, and things have changed, therefore he is okay with the motion.
Commissioner Adkinson inquired if the Board were to come back and talk about this, actually doing a study, when would that conversation happen.
Commissioner Feltner inquired if Commissioner Adkinson is asking him.
Commissioner Adkinson replied she is asking anybody.
Commissioner Feltner responded he thinks after the Board knows both the referendum, but more importantly he thinks the Legislature has said they will have implementing language in a special in December; he thinks the Board will know a lot more after that special session; and it could be done in early January.
Commissioner Adkinson inquired why the Board could not say that it was going to do a study if in fact this does pass in November.
Commissioner Feltner stated he would like to know what the implementing language is and all the other consequences that will have to be dealt with; and he advised he made his motion.
The Board directed staff to schedule a Board Agenda Item during Fiscal Year 2026-27 to consider adoption of Stormwater Utility Assessment Rate amendments following the November referendum.

title: NEW BUSINESS

action_text:
Chair Altman stated this is permission to advertise public hearing to amend the Utility Services Rate Resolution encompassing South Beaches, Merritt Island, North Brevard, Port St. John, and South Central Mainland service area.
Sandra Sullivan stated she has some heartburn because the people were first promised with the Lagoon tax for Advanced Wastewater Treatment (AWT) which is to remove the high nutrient loading, which of course goes into the wetlands and the Lagoon when the County dumps, and goes down in deep injection et cetera; the people were promised AWT with the Lagoon tax and got less than three percent of it going to that; then in 2021, there was a 46 percent compounded rate over five years to again tax the people to put money towards AWT; now, looking at another 46 percent whether it is going to be one, two, three, or five years; that works out to roughly, depending on the Board’s decision, to 113 percent increase; and she thinks there needs to be some accountability when the people have been taxed now, this will be the third iteration essentially for the same thing. She continued by saying in the last five years, 66 percent of that money was supposed to go to capital to the projects that were identified; this is from documents that the County uploaded to the Agenda Items that the Board passed; she takes issue in particular that in December 2024, there was a discussion where all of this Board promised it would not put on the rate payers, the burden of $130 million for Space Florida, but it did not keep it; now, that number is $197 million and the Board does not have funding, no State funding, and the County has doubled the money it is paying the Economic Development Commission (EDC) from $700,000 to $1.4 million when they did not deliver on bringing the money; and now this Board wants to raise the people’s rate, while Space Florida pays no property tax, as of 2026, pays no sales tax, therefore, they are not even helping to off-set what they do to the Lagoon. She noted the Board wants to insult the people by putting the cost of Space Florida’s connection to Sykes Creek on the people’s rates; and it is despicable on all of this Board as it made a commitment, Commissioner Feltner’s eyes are cast down, but this Board made a commitment that it is breaking.
Rick Heffelfinger stated he will object on the grounds that this is a mess; this packet is a mess; when he comes to the podium he pulls the information; when he looks at this Item it says the fiscal impact is an estimated minimum fiscal impact adjustments made to the water and sewer connection fees, $4.8 million; then there is a chart about how to phase it in or drop it all at once; that is great; then it says the proposed adjustment to the service fees are projected to increase $15,000 per year; he does not know where that number came from because this is all about the rate payer getting nailed, hard; and while looking at the packet he cannot create a valid timeline to figure out what the heck the County has been doing over the couple of years. He commented he thinks Ms. Sullivan just mentioned it was a couple years back and it was a progressive rate, 46 percent, and then this one drops, another 46 percent; he has no idea what the revenue actually is and this does not say; how could he approve this when he does not even know how much money it is bringing in; he does know it is bringing in a big chunk of change, like $4.8 million for the connection, it is connecting water and wastewater; he does not think it specifies there is a differentiation between a single-family residence and a mobile home park; and he asked if he were to place a mobile home park, in the future, like this, he is going to pay $8,500 for water and $4,500 for sewer; that hurts; and the previous schedule had an off-set, because that is low-income housing, or it could be his retirement home and he has a property and wants to place a mobile home on it, now he has to pay that; and that is an impact to everybody that is growing, and kind of slows people down. He added if there is no rate differential for four or five bedrooms, this bases the rate on what it was for a single-family three bedroom; it had a higher rate for four bedroom and five bedroom, and a whole lot of other stuff for condos and whatnot; he does not see any rate schedule, nail the people with $4,500 and $8,500, boom, boom, boom, everybody who builds anything; and he thinks that would be great if that was every department building and they had to pay that for each unit, that would be some serious revenue there, but it missed the big building boom. He reiterated this is a mess; he commented if he was a citizen that looked at J.1. he would say nail them, all the new people, then to look at it and say, “Wow, what are you going to do to those mobile home people.”; this is misguided from the get go and it is a screwed up package; he would say dismiss this and bring it back with the right documentation; one cannot even get a clear copy of the previous Resolutions, they are half marked up from one year; and it is terrible.
Edward Fontanin, Utility Services Director, stated this is to get permission to advertise the rate resolution and he will touch a little bit on the revisions and tie that in with the fiscal impact as was mentioned previously; in the resolution staff did some cleanup work with regard to some of the definitions and some of the languages; as it associates to the fiscal impact associated with server fees in Exhibit B, those are really related to water turnoff and towing fees that were just adjusted from $55 to $75, minor incremental service fees that are done for the residents; with regard to the connection fees, they do function as impact fees; these are the fees associated with growth; this is for new construction, nothing is related to the existing rate payers because once one pays the connection fee once it is for perpetuity; and the intent of this is understanding what the growth is in Brevard County and making the adjustment. He noted they went through an analysis to determine what the appropriate rate would be for now, today, in order to make sure that future development are paying their fair share of what the growth or the expansion of utilities would be needed; with regard to the line item, on the exhibit, when it comes to different criteria of development, whether a restaurant, mobile home, or whatnot, what was previously in the Resolution that went back 25 years, there was a table in there that was not correct; in the exhibit of the rate resolution, it is referencing the Florida Administrative Code 62-2.008, and this is what the State of Florida uses as the ratio of homes; it is a reference, the starting point of the connection fee is a reference to a one to two bedroom home; but, depending on if it is bigger entity or smaller entity, it would be listed in the Florida Administrative Code 62-6.008, that staff would use as the guidance to provide the correct ratio and the adjustment of any connection fee for other than a single-family home.
Commissioner Adkinson stated the County has not had an increase since 1993, and she is wondering why; and she asked if this is making the County come in line to comply with some Federal standards, not just increasing because it feels like it.
Mr. Fontanin replied this is basically in order to provide for future development there has to be expansion of capacity in order to service that; this fee is a calculation for every equivalent single-family home; and equivalent is what the initial payment would be for the capital cost to provide the capital for the Department to provide that expansion.
Commissioner Adkinson asked why the fees have not gone up since 1993.
Mr. Fontanin responded by saying it has not been brought to the Board and this is staff’s opportunity to get it corrected.
Chair Altman highlighted one point, these are connection fees in effect, not an impact fee because it is a connection fee; there is a legal difference; and this is looking at growth paying for growth.
Mr. Fontanin responded affirmatively. He inquired if staff could get some guidance in terms of advertisement on which of these options; and he noted they are just suggestions and if any of the Commissioners wish to talk on the different options, they may.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she is wondering if the County did a phased approach, would it need the money right now, or if doing a phased approach, is that sufficient to get them where they need to be.
Mr. Fontanin replied by saying he thinks obviously, the sooner it gets done the better because as construction costs are going up every year, it may have an impact on this; but, going with a phased approach is still getting the rates in the right position.
Chair Altman stated option 1 is adjust fee once from current fee to full amount of the recommended fee; two, spread increase over two years to achieve recommended amount; three, spread increase over three years to achieve the recommended amount; four, spread the increase over five years to the recommended amount; and five, any additional direction provided by the Board. He mentioned maybe while the Board is thinking about this, what is the real life impact of spreading it out or putting it at full year, option 1.
Mr. Fontanin stated the more it is spread out, every new home, every new connection that is on the service, that is a lost opportunity for the adjusted rate; that is really the impact of it; there is one opportunity when it comes to getting a connection fee; once that connection fee is paid, as long as that structure remains the same, the connection fee is paid per perpetuity; staff is comfortable with the phased approach as has been shown here; and they will take direction from the Board.
Chair Altman stated so it is a big fee up front and done or just a recurring fee that is going to be coming.
Mr. Fontanin explained it is a one-time fee and it is typically paid by the contractor, not the homeowner.
Chair Altman asked if it is a phased approach it is going to be paid over a two year period; and he asked if Mr. Fontanin would explain the phased approach.
Mr. Fontanin explained the phased approach would be it if was done over per se three years, whoever builds or is asking for a connection fee in year one are going to pay that amount and that is it; whoever builds in the year two period would pay that amount; whoever pays in year one would not pay the fee in year two or three; as he said, the longer it is spread out, the people in year one or two are paying that connection fee, staff does not go back and say…
Chair Altman interrupted by saying he understands; and he asked what the disadvantage is to spreading it out.
Mr. Fontanin advised the disadvantage is just a form of loss revenue; the calculation that staff has come up with is the $8,500 and the $4,500 for water and sewer; and it is just receiving a lesser revenue because they are getting it at a reduced rate because of the phased out approach.
Chair Altman asked what the impact is of lesser revenue.
Mr. Fontanin replied that is a function that is quite honestly a function to the amount of connection fees for that given year; but as he said, given where they were currently today, if the Board does decide to do it over a period of time staff is comfortable that once it gets to the desired rate that they will be in a better position than they would be today.
Chair Altman commented the Board has a few options.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she would like to make a motion; and she advised people cannot talk from audience.
Chair Altman stated the Board will finish the dialogue it is having amongst the staff.
Mr. Fontanin stated by no means does this say this study or Agenda is associated with water or sewer user rates.
Chair Altman stated if Mr. Heffelfinger wants to ask a couple more questions to come on up.
Mr. Heffelfinger stated to direct attention to Exhibit B, it is redlined; go to page 12 and one will see this is taking a base charge of $17.40 for a five-eighths meter, taking it from $17.40 to $25.40; it is taking a one inch line from $29 to $42; then that fee covers for 3,000 gallons on the five-eighths and that covers for 5,000; then there is the overage; the rate has a scale, and all those scales have increased; tier one went from $5.44 to $7.96; the people that are paying the water bill are getting nailed by this; and he asked if that is true or false.
Mr. Fontanin explained when this Resolution was approved in 2022, it was also approved with an annual index; every time staff goes through and does an update to the rate resolution, they are merely taking those rates to the current of the indexed amount that was already preapproved by the Board, rather than go back and provide a rate resolution that was referencing 2021; and the fees are redlined, however, the fees are appropriate on the annual index that was approved by the Board and not a penny more.
Mr. Heffelfinger inquired if this is just a restatement of what was done in 2022.
Mr. Fontanin responded in the affirmative.
Mr. Heffelfinger asked if there is no rate increase on the users, that this is a result of the phased four years that Ms. Sullivan was talking about; and it is not a user rate fee, it is just the connection. He commented he does not know why this was in there, it is confusing; he guesses maybe Mr. Fontanin took the opportunity to fix the 2022 Resolution; he does not know what the original 2022 Resolution looked like, it looks as though staff marked up one from 2013 and then half marked up the one from 2022 to this year; and he does not think the Resolution was ever right. He went on to say this is so confusing that now staff had him and Ms. Sullivan thinking that the Board is raising user rates, but it is not; everybody understood that; and he does not understand why these documents were in there.
Chair Altman asked if Ms. Sullivan had a question.
Ms. Sullivan stated she did not print it out to bring it here; what she read in the document, the rates that were increased in the last five years were 9.5 percent, then 8.5 percent, then 8.5, 8.5, then 7.5; it says after that, each year after that will be Consumer Price Index (CPI); she is pretty good at reading this stuff; she is pretty sure it was talking about a rate increase on the water usage and sewer usage; she will go back and dig into it because this Board even talked up here about increasing the rates; and she is all for the impact fee part of it being up and presumably this is coming out of that impact fee study. She went on to ask if there is a report that should have been attached where these numbers came from.
Chair Altman stated he thinks this was separate from that, it is a connection fee.
Ms. Sullivan argued no, he said this is essentially an impact fee, and she asked so is this from the impact fee feasibility study.
Chair Altman interjected by saying let him explain the difference between a rate and an impact…
Mr. Fontanin asked Chair Altman to repeat.
Chair Altman stated this is not from the impact fee study, this is a rate increase.
Mr. Fontanin stated this was an independent exercise that staff did as Utility Services beyond what the County is doing from the collective.
Chair Altman stated there is a technical difference between a rate increase, he knows it is a legal thing, in the vernacular they are the same, but there is a legal difference.
Commissioner Adkinson stated without being a builder or a contractor, like Mr. Fontanin was saying, if the Board were to do the progressive approach, then all of the connection fees in the first year, they will be paying less than those in year three or five; she is in the opinion of doing it all at once or two years; and that is where she is at.
Chair Altman stated he agrees with that; if the Board is going to do it, it might as well get it done in the most efficient way and go with year one; then of course if there is a fallback, two years would be the second best.
Commissioner Adkinson advised she is prepared to make a motion if the Chair is willing to entertain it.
Chair Altman stated the audience member said the chart does not show the year one rates.
Mr. Fontanin stated that is correct, however they do state what they are within the Agenda Report.
Chair Altman asked for that number to be provided before the vote.
Mr. Fontanin stated the numbers are $8,500 and $4,500; when looking at the chart, in any implementation plan, it always gets to the total of $8,500 and $4,500, so it is really a question of when the Board wants to achieve that; and he thinks the discussion is one year.
The Board granted permission to advertise a Public Hearing to consider amendments to the Utility Service Rates Resolution and its Exhibits; and approved implementation of Option 1, adjusting the fees once from the current fees to full amount of recommended fees.

Edward Fontanin, Utility Services Director, stated this is legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance to sunset the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District on December 31, 2029; the background behind this, the last bond payment for Barefoot Bay is December 2029; in December 2029 there will be no debt service associated with the District and as a result while currently working on the replacement of the water and wastewater plant of Barefoot Bay, that will actually be outside of the District; compound that with the fact that the legislature of the mandate related to discharges and the integrity of pipes and whatnot; it also gets restrictive in the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District because it is a dependent district which means they can only spend what they generate within that district; and the way staff sees it is debt service at the 2029 will be paid off, it will be transferred over to the Countywide system, which is still currently operating, and it will give staff more freedom to transfer money for expenditures that are needed within the district without the financial confines of the dependent district.
Sydne James stated the information she has provided the Board is a good faith estimate of accurate data that she was able to research; she has focused in her document on base wastewater rates because Barefoot Bay water rates are similar to other communities, but the wastewater rates are not; the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer system was purchased in 2000 from the Florida Governmental Utility Authority; the residential customers who are serviced by it are the only customers in unincorporated Brevard County who pay for their own specific water treatment plant; it is neither fair nor equitable; the base wastewater rate for approximately 5,000 Barefoot Bay customers is currently $54.28, and for the other 69,400 residential customers in unincorporated Brevard County it is $28.17; and the Agenda Item tonight is to integrate into the Countywide system on December 31, 2029, after the current debt obligation is fulfilled, the question of when to make this happen, integrating them, should not be about current Barefoot Bay debt, it should be about deciding when to eliminate the inequity, the disparity, the unfairness, call it whatever, it is all of these things that the Barefoot Bay water and sewer plant have to be burdened by only 5,000 residents when the other five plants serviced by 69,400 residential customers get to divide that up amongst so many more people. She went on to say the roll back to 2025 rates indicate in the press release that it amounts to a decrease of only $2.66 per month on sewer rates; it is too small of an amount to have any meaningful relief; if Barefoot Bay was immediately integrated into the Countywide system, the customers, everybody else except Barefoot Bay, base sewer rates would increase by approximately $1.58 per month, not even noticeable, but Barefoot bay would decrease from $54.28 or the proposed lower rate of $51.62 to only $29.75; this decrease would make a profound impact to the lives of many customers in Barefoot Bay, especially those who only live on Social Security income and are struggling to get by; the residents are not asking for a handout, or special treatment, all they are asking is for the Board to remove the yoke tying them to the Barefoot Bay District and to be treated like all the other residential customers in unincorporated Brevard County; many cannot bear the heavy weight of this yoke for three and one-half more years; and she asked the Board to please do it now or at the very latest December 31, 2026.
John Requa stated he has been to the Board twice and said the same thing, but Ms. James said it more eloquently; he has spoken to the Director before and sent him by registered mail, four questions that he never got answers to; he noted the questions were what was the price of the bond when he started, how much has been paid in, how much do the residents own, and did they receive the upgrades that he told were part of the deal with the bond; he would really like to have those questions answered; the other thing is for Commissioner Adkinson to hold true to what she said in the Tatler of October 2025, the cost of the bond should be spread across the District; they are District 3, Barefoot Bay does not own that facility, they do not run that facility, the County does; that is what they are asking and that is what legal counsel has asked her from Barefoot Bay; and that is all the residents want. He went on to say people are suffering under these fees, and people are leaving; the price of water, homeowners of modular homes, taxes, the Board is going to turn Palm Bay into a trailer park and then maybe Ashton Park to take it over; that is how bad the residents are hurt; he hopes the Board listens to him and responds; Ms. James is absolutely correct in saying to spread the cost of the bond over the District, that is all the residents want; he does not have any hope in a new plant or in that reducing the prices because he does not believe it one bit; and he has no reason to see any good merit that is going to come when the Board will not listen to the people and will not act on their pleas. He noted he will surrender the rest of his time as he has said twice before.
Adriane Pearl stated she lives in Barefoot Bay and she would like to address the monthly rising cost of the water bills; she believes they are being estimated; there have been several customers getting $200 and $300 bills that are older couples; they do not understand why their bills are so high, they go to the water company and are told they have leaks; they gets plumbers to come out and there are no leaks; she is on Social Security Disability and lives on $1,400 per month which is not easy especially with the rising cost of insurance; she has the same routine every month, she does not do anything differently, and she is a one-person household; residents are being told that there is one meter reader for approximately 5,000 homes in their District; and there is no way one person, even with the new digital meters can get to 5,000 homes to read these meters. She noted she has three bills here, May, June, and July; May and June were $92.59, the exact same amount and the exact same water usage; she finds that to be physically impossible, one cannot use the exact same amount every month for two months in a row; in July, her bill jumped from $92.59 to $100.08; what she has found is happening is every two months she is receiving duplicate bills and the third month it is arbitrarily raised anywhere from $8 to $10 a month; when she first moved to Barefoot Bay her bill was $50, and now she is looking at over $100; she is literally drowning, she cannot afford it any longer; and she is asking the Board to address this community and try to do what the customers are asking it to do if at all possible because they cannot afford $200 to $300 water bills. She mentioned as of next year, this is totally not within the scope here, but as of next year with the insurance crisis because everyone is under Citizens Property Insurance Corporation, she is probably going to lose her home as she is paying $4,000 right now; next year they are going to have the flood assessment even though she is not in a flood district; these bills are getting astronomical and ludicrous; something has to be done; there are a lot of lower income families there and she would like for Commissioner Adkinson, if possible, to address the fact of how many exact employees are reading the meters; one of the ladies told them that they were short staffed and they did not know what to tell people; and she would appreciate that.
Sandra Sullivan stated one of the things Commissioner Delaney brought to this Board, which she really appreciated, was her transparency; when it comes to this, District 3 is in the process, and was just approved buying a parcel next to this facility to presumably put in a toilet to tap, sewage to drinking water facility; that was estimated to be $319 million if she recalls correctly from last year; when she looked legislatively what counties are asking for, what she did not see for Brevard is any appropriation requests to any of the State Representatives for that; obviously, if the burden keeps being placed on the people, because to their point, Barefoot Bay, when the people had the increases, hers was 46 percent over five years, she did not calculate Barefoot Bay’s, theirs was way more; they were like over 10 percent a year increases; and she asked if the rest of the County, for sewage and the water systems, at the same rate. She continued to say the County has certain plants that are in worse condition, sewage plants on that side, that is not sewage it is water, but even up in Titusville the water plant, there was something on the Agenda to night; there are issues with plants, water, sewage, and different areas of critical needs to be addressed; she asked to that point is there validity, it is just a thought to have everybody on the same rate for equity; she mentioned the County manages things; it took it over; she remembers the vote when the County took over that facility as Special District; it does not need to be a Special District waiting until 2029; and she asked if there is a way to get out of that earlier. She mentioned she questions more than anything, given the comments that have been made because it is a very high rate compared to what everybody else has; she would like to see some transparency regarding the County’s plans for funding the new facility because this Agenda Item says this plan is at the end of its life; it cannot be recouped and kept going, it is end of life; and she inquired what is the replacement plan, how does the County plan to fund it, and what is going to be done to try to mitigate that so it does not all end up on the people.
Rick Heffelfinger stated this is Utility Services Department again; this whole water situation, he has never been able to understand how many water plants, who pays for them, how people are rate increased, and how they are not; he does not know who controls this one; it sounds like the Barefoot Bay facility is part of the big Brevard system, but they are obviously charging different fees; now it turns out the County is going to sunset them after they pay off their debt, but they are going to collect fees from now until then; he would guess they have not been saving anything for a plant because the plant is shot; he asked if there is a fund that accumulated money so they can give it to Brevard County so that it can work on that other plant; and he commented he does not know what that other plant is. He asked why not shut this plant down run a pipe to the new plant and just put that one over capacity as well; he mentioned he does not know if this one is over capacity; he inquired if it is still one million gallons per day or if it has been upgraded from that; he commented he does not know; the chart on the County page, he already knows it is out-of-date because it says they were going to have the South/Central Park completed in 2019; well it was, it is at $12 million so this has not been updated, therefore, he cannot use the County web page to figure anything out; when he tries to figure out what is going on, but he did pull these service billing rates, and this is the most convoluted thing; he even tried to figure out what zone and area that he is in and there is no connection fee or anything; he does not know if anybody is building a new place in Barefoot Bay; and he asked if they are going to get those connection fees as well. He inquired if there are any empty properties in there; he stated the County could get some serious cash just by nailing them with those connection fees right there; that might go into the coffers; he does not know why the Board is waiting to pay off debt as they are collecting services and not placing any of that service fee money into an account because they have not maintained it, the plant is dead, it is way past use, and nothing was reinvested; and he asked if that was staffs job to reinvest, or the Board’s job to reinvest. He stated he does not know what they did if they just stood around and managed it; and the water system here sucks.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she has a couple questions; she understands that the new plant down there is going to service Barefoot Bay, Snug Harbor, and the rest of the residents who need servicing; and she asked if Mr. Fontanin can tell her what the total debt is for Barefoot Bay, currently.
Mr. Fontanin replied he believes it is somewhere around $4 million, but he will have to double check that.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if Mr. Fontanin can tell her very briefly how that debt occurred.
Mr. Fontanin explained that Barefoot Bay from its existence was operated as a development with their own private water sewer system; he thinks late '60s or early '70s where this occurred, as they grew, his understanding is around mid to late '90s, the people of Barefoot Bay were complaining of the service that the private utility was providing them; based on that, and he does not know much detail, it made it to the Board and the Board in '97 or '99 agreed to bring Barefoot Bay as part of the County system on the condition that it be done as a Dependent District; why it was decided to do it as a Dependent District, he does not have the background; and however, he thinks there was discussion that there was fear back in '93 that the people of Barefoot Bay were concerned that the revenue generated there would go to other areas.
Commissioner Adkinson remarked that is how the debt happened and that is how it was incurred.
Mr. Fontanin stated in order for the County to get ownership of the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District, there was an amount that had to be paid to that entity of $25 or $30 million in order for that transaction to occur.
Commissioner Adkinson stated clearly she has heard tonight that people would like to just be on the County system because they feel that it will be better; her question would be can Mr. Fontanin sit down with her behind closed doors and help her to concoct an argument that she can give to the rest of the Board, how to convince them that all of the other residents in Brevard County should take on this debt; and she asked if Mr. Fontanin could help her with that argument.
Mr. Fontanin advised he thinks that is more of a legal question about how user rates in the Countywide system can be used in that regard; and he can have a further conversation with her.
Commissioner Adkinson stated maybe that is a County Attorney, Morris Richardson, question if it is about legality; and she apologized for placing attorney Richardson on the spot.
Attorney Richardson stated he thinks she is absolutely right about the discussion that happened back then; it was viewed by the County Commission and County residents as a bailout of this private system, so they did not want to wall it off; they created that District, but because of the bond issue, the revenue bonds do not constitute a debt liability or obligation of the County, they are an obligation of being paid solely from the revenues that are generated from the District; and that is part of the reason that even if the Board were inclined to forget the history and the bailout, try to rest and make things on equal standing. He noted they cannot use revenue from other parts of the County system to pay off those bonds; those bonds have to be payable and secured; the rates have to be sufficient; it violates the bond covenants if the rate were not set at a sufficient amount to service that debt; that is why Mr. Fontanin had to do the study; while he was trying to get them some relief, the study sets the parameters of what relief it can afford, but still generate enough revenue to be able to satisfy and service that bond; now, fortunately they are very close to the end of that road; it has been a long time when that was established, 1999; and it will be 30 years in 2029. He mentioned that by providing an ordinance that sunsets the District now and then following up with a rate resolution that affords whatever relief that it can, which is rolling back the rates somewhat, but also freezing those rates at that rolled back rate so they do not continue to escalate every year; and there will come a point when its sunset where it will be rolled in with a new plant and one Countywide rate.
Commissioner Adkinson stated so legally they cannot.
Attorney Richardson advised right now, legally, because of the structure of the debt and the bond obligations, the debt service has to be generated out of the District.
Commissioner Adkinson stated her next point is, and she asked because she is hearing Barefoot Bay, if Mr. Fontanin could make it better for them rather than what was originally continuing to rise over the next years; and he checked, did some recalculations, and he is telling her it can be rolled back and frozen for a while.
Mr. Fontanin stated assuming the Board goes down the path to approve sunsetting Barefoot Bay, then calculate the user rate for Barefoot Bay, the calculation changes because it is no longer an entity for perpetuity, it would be an entity for four years; staff has done that where it can roll it back to the 2025 rates and flat line it from that point on until the sunset period; she knows the Commissioner asked him the question and the Assistant County Manager, Jill Hayes, fact checked it for him, and the answer is there is $4.5 million left in the bond.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she does not know the answer to this; and she asked if the costs are estimated, if someone is reading the meter monthly, or how does that work in Barefoot Bay.
Mr. Fontanin replied one of the things that have been done in Barefoot Bay, the County has taken over the really old utility, so they have invested in replacing all the residential water meters; he stated it is all by radio reading; one person can do more than 5,000 readings because all it consists of is driving down the road at 25 to 30 miles per hour and it records it; there is ample personnel in order to do that; and if any of the residents have a discrepancy in the bill, please let the Department know.
Commissioner Adkinson stated if anybody has a serious concern about bills being wildly wrong, if they brought them to her they can clearly bring them to staff; but if they brought them to her, she could also bring them to Mr. Fontanin.
Mr. Fontanin replied affirmatively.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if he would look at them specifically.
Mr. Fontanin responded affirmatively stating and because of the radio read, it provides a diurnal of what the water flow is; he is a homeowner, he had a high water bill, he had the water department pull it from the water meter, and the guy asked him literally if he was throwing parties at 2:00 a.m. because he had a slow leak; and staff has that data now to check that.
Ms. Pearl stated she would someone to clarify if the people can read their own meters; she does nothing they are being read; the maintenance department hangs out under the trees all day and they still get paid; she does not see how elderly couples have bills of $200 to $300; like she said early her routines never changed in the six years that she has been there; and it started at $50, now it is $100; and she would like to know if the people can read their own meters.
Mr. Fontanin stated it is not like an old school meter where it has a dial on it and people could actually read the numbers, it is all electronic; if any resident wants to see the data of that, the Department can provide it; for the circumstances, staff gets a variety of issues or dynamics associated with bills so it would be tough to say this is reason for any high bills.
Ms. Pearl asked how people would go about requesting that data monthly.
Mr. Fontanin advised to contact the billing office.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if one would just need to contact the billing office to request that.
Mr. Fontanin responded affirmatively.
Ms. James asked if she may give Commissioner Adkinson a tiny bit of that argument of why the other Commissioners might want to go along with this plan; she mentioned both groups would have more residential customers to share the cost associated with repair and maintenance throughout the County; it is truly a win-win; she knows the Board is creative and imaginative; she believes the Board members have a strong moral compass to do the right thing; she thinks the Board can figure out how to pay this debt off and create a new one; and it is barely anything more to the residential customers throughout unincorporated Brevard County, but for the Barefoot Bay residents it would have a profound impact.
Commissioner Feltner stated he also had a small leak and was able to turn everything off to the house and see the digital meter that there was still flow; he was able to find it and have someone come out and fix it; it was not terrible for them; and he asked if the residents can do that with their meters. He inquired if the meters are digital to see that in real time.
Mr. Fontanin noted the radio read meters provide an actual diurnal and he cannot remember but he thinks it holds two or three weeks so they can actually look and see what the water usage is on a 24-hour period over that duration to see.
Commissioner Adkinson commented so they know they have turned everything off, like what Commissioner Feltner is saying, if they know on specific days or whatever that they have turned everything off; and she asked if someone asked for a particular day, staff can see if there is still usage.
Mr. Fontanin responded in the affirmative.
Kevin Heal stated his question is how is it all being managed; all the sites that he has seen all over Brevard County, Florida, and all over the country, he does not think anyone really knows where they have been strategically placed them; water pipes are breaking everywhere; he sees leaks everywhere he goes; the infrastructure is really bad and the County has to protect the people; someone could be tampering with that stuff, water is water; he does not want to go crazy but Iran and all that stuff is going on, and the County has to be careful and protect the people at all cost; and he wants the Board to think about that, how important the infrastructure is. He commented maybe something can be done where the whole State works together to fix this issue.
Chair Altman stated this is a very difficult issue; he remembers when he first came on the Commission in '84, the Commission had just completed implementation of the Clean Water Act; if one multiplies this problem by probably 100 or maybe 1,000, that was the magnitude of the issue they had to deal with; there was dozens of rickety, rackety old sewer treatment, water treatment plants that developers had put in, in the '60s when the wild, wild west was trying to build for the Apollo program; and they had to clean them all up. He noted they had massive rate increases; he does not know if they had averaged those rates; when they built Sykes Creek and the South Beaches plan, he does not know if they were able to combine the rates to share the impact of the overall cleanup; the question, can they average in with the rest of the County, he thought of that historic time; there was a massive rate increase but they did fix the problem; hats off to the County Commission back in the '70s and '80s, it made it a lot easier for its predecessors; and he just wonders if there is any precedent there in the way they handled that, that could be applied today.
Attorney Richardson stated he is reading the minutes from the meeting and it is the exact same discussion about the equity of the rates, where the base rate in Barefoot Bay is higher; their water use on average is lower, but because the base rate is higher, they still at the time had a higher overall bill than customers outside of the system; the issue was all about what the County inherited with that system that they took over and, bailed out was the term that kept being used back then, and the debt associated with that; there are bond obligations that the County has to comply with, that is why everything is staked to the retirement of the debt; and that is when things can be leveled out and they can come in and be part of the Countywide system.
Chair Altman stated eventually they can get there but not initially.
Attorney Richardson stated this ordinance is the first step to that because it puts a sunset on it establishes a hard date at which the District will be dissolved, when the debt is satisfied.
Chair Altman commented they may achieve it ultimately.
Attorney Richardson noted this is an affirmative statement by the Board that they will get there and when.
Mr. Heal stated the Board mentioned the slow leaking data, and he asked about the large leaking date; he has seen in different areas and all over the State, not just Florida, where there is water running slow leaks and fast leaks and no checking on it for days, months; and he asked who is paying for that.
Commissioner Adkinson stated if there is no further discussion she would like to make the motion to approve legislative intent set forth below and direct staff to prepare an ordinance implementing the intent and schedule and advertise the ordinance for public hearing.
The Board approved legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance to sunset the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District on December 31, 2029; and directed staff to draft the ordinance.
body: Brevard County Board of County Commissioners
matter_type: New Business - Development and Environmental Services Group
title: Legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance sunsetting the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District on December 31, 2029, while honoring the existing contractual obligations and commitments of the District.

action_text:
Juanita Jackson, Housing and Human Services Director, stated this Item is the creation of the Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee and amending to the Together in Partnership (TIP) Citizen Advisory Committee to remove opioid funding and responsibilities; on December 7, 2021, the Board approved an amendment to the TIP Resolution to establish two subcommittees, including representation from the municipalities; under the TIP Advisory Board, the two subcommittees were charged with making suggestions on which approved uses to address and fund with opioid settlement funding, oversee the Request for Application (RFA) process, and make funding recommendations to the Board; after several years of administering opioid settlement funds, Housing and Human Services proposes removing the opioid review and recommendations committee from the TIP Advisory Board structure and establish a standalone advisory committee to be known as, the Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee; this will be in line with the our Advisory Committees; and the Opioid Misuse Advisory Committee shall serve as an advisory committee to the Board and to County Administration regarding planning, implementation, and oversight of opioid settlement funding activities. She continued by saying the structure will be as such to make sure Brevard County remains a qualified County; a representative from the City of Melbourne, City of Palm Bay, a representative from Space Coast League of Cities, a representative from Brevard County Government, a representative from Brevard County Sheriff’s Department, and the four remaining at-large seats will be chosen as citizens from the community involvement; and with the approval of the creation of Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee as a separate standalone advisory committee, it is further requested that the existing Opioid Review and Recommendation Subcommittees be removed from TIP, including the standing committee seats that were added for the qualified County purposes.
The Board adopted Resolution No. 26-054, establishing the creation of Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee, and Resolution No. 26-055, amending the TIP Citizen Advisory Committee, upon approval by the County Attorney and Risk Management.
